sentences.text: This predator featured a deep, laterally compressed skull equipped with large, blade-like teeth.
Its snout was notably shorter and lower than those of related baurusuchids.
The upper margin of the skull sat lower than the back, creating a distinct, slightly sloping profile.
A small depression on the premaxilla bone held the first lower tooth when the jaws closed.
Holes at the back of the skull, known as supratemporal fenestrae, were relatively small in size.
Fossils representing four partial skulls were unearthed in the Honorópolis District of the Adamantina Formation.
The genus was first named in 2011 by a research team including Ismar De Souza Carvalho and Vicente De Paula Antunes Teixeira.
The generic name combines 'Campina', the location of discovery, with 'suchus', referring to the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
The species name 'diniz' honors Izonel Queiroz Diniz Neto and the Diniz and Martins Queiroz families, who owned the farm where the fossils were found.
Campinasuchus was a fully terrestrial predator, behaving similarly to other members of the baurusuchid group.
Taxonomically, Campinasuchus belongs to the parent group Pissarrachampsinae.
It is classified within the family Baurusuchidae.
This animal lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
